verses.text: “Watch your step: don’t do your good deeds just to get people looking at you. Then there’ll be no reward from your Father in heaven.”
“So when you give to people in need, don’t make a whole announcement about it like the hypocrites do in synagogues and on the streets to get praise. They’ve already got the reward they wanted.”
“When you help someone, don’t even let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,”
“so your giving stays private. Your Father sees what happens in secret and will reward you openly.”
“When you pray, don’t copy the hypocrites. They love standing in synagogues and street corners praying for an audience. They’ve got the reward they wanted.”
“But when you pray, go into your room, close the door, and pray to your Father who’s unseen. Your Father sees what happens in secret and will reward you openly.”
“When you pray, don’t pile up empty words like the nations do. They think all that talking will get them heard.”
“Don’t be like them. Your Father already knows what you need before you ask him.”
“Pray like this: ‘Our Father in heaven, let your name be honored as holy.”
“Let your Kingdom come; let your will happen on earth just as it does in heaven.”
“Give us today the bread we need for today.”
“Forgive what we owe, just as we forgive those who owe us.”
“Don’t let us fall into temptation; rescue us from the evil one. The Kingdom, power, and glory are yours forever. Amen.’”
“If you forgive people for the wrongs they do, your Father in heaven will forgive you too.”
“But if you won’t forgive people, your Father won’t forgive your wrongs either.”
“When you fast, don’t put on a gloomy face like the hypocrites. They make themselves look miserable so people will notice they’re fasting. They’ve got their reward already.”
“But when you fast, put oil on your head and wash your face,”
“so people won’t know you’re fasting—only your Father, who’s unseen. Your Father sees what happens in secret and will reward you openly.”
“Don’t stack up treasure for yourself on earth, where moths and rust wreck it and thieves break in and steal.”
“Stack up treasure in heaven instead, where moths and rust can’t wreck it and thieves can’t break in and steal.”
“Where your treasure is, that’s where your heart will be too.”
“The eye is the body’s lamp. If your eye is healthy, your whole body is full of light.”
“But if your eye is unhealthy, your whole body is full of darkness. If the light inside you is actually darkness, that darkness is deep.”
“Nobody can serve two masters. You’ll hate one and love the other, or stay loyal to one and look down on the other. You can’t serve both God and money.”
“So here’s what I’m telling you: don’t stress over your life—what you’ll eat or drink—or over your body and what you’ll wear. Isn’t life more than food, and your body more than clothes?”
“Look at the birds in the sky: they don’t plant, harvest, or store food in barns, yet your Father in heaven feeds them. Aren’t you worth more than they are? 🐦”
“Can any of you add even one moment to your life by worrying?”
“And why stress about clothes? Look at the wild lilies and how they grow. They don’t work or spin thread,”
“but I’m telling you, even Solomon at his most glorious wasn’t dressed like one of them.”
“If God dresses the field’s grass like this—even though it’s here today and thrown into the oven tomorrow—won’t he take care of you even more, you of little faith?”
“So don’t spiral asking, ‘What are we going to eat?’ ‘What are we going to drink?’ or ‘What are we going to wear?’”
“The nations chase after all that stuff. Your Father in heaven knows you need it.”
“Put God’s Kingdom and his righteousness first, and all those things will be given to you too.”
“So don’t stress about tomorrow. Tomorrow can handle its own worries. Today already has enough trouble.”
